designSummary: Cross-classification of index test and reference standard in randomly sampled messages from three clinics.
sampleSize: With sensitivity near 86 percent and urgent messages at about 4 percent, about 95 urgent messages give a 95 percent confidence interval of about 7 percentage points either side of the estimate; at 4 percent that means about 2,400 sampled messages, or about 12 weeks at 200 messages per week across three clinics. Reporting sensitivity by clinic with an interval of about 12 points either side needs about 32 urgent messages per clinic.
primaryAnalysis: Sensitivity and specificity with Wilson intervals, overall and by clinic, from the two-by-two table against the adjudicated reference standard.
secondaryAnalysis: Sensitivity for messages in languages other than English and from patients over 75; kappa before adjudication; description of every false negative.
missingData: Messages the flag failed to score are counted and reported; they are treated as not flagged in a sensitivity analysis.
multiplicity: One primary measure; subgroups are descriptive with intervals.
overfittingGuards: No threshold tuning of the flag
summary: About 95 urgent messages from about 2,400 sampled over 12 weeks.
